question: Can an iPhone run Google Live Transcribe?
slides: Google's Live Transcribe is an *Android feature.*
description: An iPhone owner who searches for Google Live Transcribe will not find a Google app by that name, because Google documents it as a feature of Android phones.
Google's Android Accessibility Help describes Live Transcribe as preinstalled on Pixel phones and some other Android phones.
In November 2026 a search of Apple's US App Store for live transcribe listed an app of that name made by Mighty Fine Apps LLC, not by Google.
Captio AI is made for deaf and hard of hearing people and runs on iPhone and Android, so a family with both phones can share one app.
Google's help page for Live Transcribe says an internet connection is needed unless you pick one of the offline languages.
Without a connection, Captio AI can still record and transcribes the recording once the phone is online again, but live captions need internet.
Google says you can find Live Transcribe's transcription history for up to three days, while Captio AI keeps recordings and their audio in a searchable library.
Ask people before you save a conversation as a recording.
On an Android phone, Live Transcribe is the better pick when you want captions in downloaded offline languages, according to Google's help page.
Captions in Captio AI can contain mistakes, and the app does not replace an interpreter or a human captioner.
